subject.title: fix: plugin host commands leave orphan child processes after timeout

question: Should `runPluginCommandWithTimeout` adopt process-tree termination as an unconditional plugin SDK behavior, or must it expose the same explicit `killProcessTree: false` opt-out that the runtime facade preserves?
rationale: This is a public plugin-facing default change with upgrade consequences; source inspection cannot determine whether plugin authors may rely on descendants surviving a timeout.

options.title: Add a helper opt-out
options.body: Add `killProcessTree?: boolean` to the helper options, default it to true, preserve explicit false, and cover both paths with focused tests.

options.title: Approve an unconditional helper default
options.body: Document maintainer approval that all helper callers should have their descendants terminated on timeout or abort, despite having no opt-out.

recommendation.title: Add a helper opt-out
recommendation.body: Add `killProcessTree?: boolean` to the helper options, default it to true, preserve explicit false, and cover both paths with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related proposal and this PR's stated scope comparison make them the strongest available routing candidate for the process-tree default discussion.
